sanskrit: athovāca mahātejā harirājo mahābalaḥ kim iyaṃ vyathitā senā mūḍhavāteva naur jale
english: Then the great-spirited lord of monkeys, greatly powerful, spoke: "Why is this army distressed, like a ship tossed on water by a confused wind?"

sanskrit: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā vāliputro 'ṅgado 'bravīt na tvaṃ paśyasi rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Having heard the words of Sugrīva, Aṅgada son of Vālin said: "You do not see Rāma, nor Lakṣmaṇa of great might,

sanskrit: śarajālācitau vīrāv ubhau daśarathātmajau śaratalpe mahātmānau śayānau rudhirokṣitau
english: The two heroes, both sons of Daśaratha, covered over with a net of arrows — those two great-souled ones lying on a bed of shafts, drenched with blood."

sanskrit: athābravīd vānarendraḥ sugrīvaḥ putram aṅgadam nānimittam idaṃ manye bhavitavyaṃ bhayena tu
english: Then Sugrīva, lord of the vānaras, spoke to his son Aṅgada: "I do not think this [distress] is without cause — there must be something to fear.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇavadanā hy ete tyaktapraharaṇā diśaḥ prapalāyanti harayas trāsād utphullalocanāḥ
english: For see — these monkeys with downcast faces, having abandoned their weapons, flee in all directions out of terror, their eyes wide open with fright.

sanskrit: anyonyasya na lajjante na nirīkṣanti pṛṣṭhataḥ viprakarṣanti cānyonyaṃ patitaṃ laṅghayanti ca
english: They feel no shame before one another, they do not look back behind them; they push each other aside and leap over the fallen."

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīro gadāpāṇir vibhīṣaṇaḥ sugrīvaṃ vardhayām āsa rāghavaṃ ca niraikṣata
english: At that moment the hero Vibhīṣaṇa, mace in hand, greeted Sugrīva and then looked toward Rāghava.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaṃ taṃ sugrīvo dṛṣṭvā vānarabhīṣaṇam ṛkṣarājaṃ samīpasthaṃ jāmbavantam uvāca ha
english: Seeing that Vibhīṣaṇa, who struck terror into the monkeys, Sugrīva spoke to Jāmbavān, the king of bears, who stood nearby:

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇo 'yaṃ saṃprāpto yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānararṣabhāḥ vidravanti paritrastā rāvaṇātmajaśaṅkayā
english: "This one who has arrived is Vibhīṣaṇa, upon seeing whom the foremost of monkeys scatter in utter terror, suspecting him to be Rāvaṇa's son.

sanskrit: śīghram etān suvitrastān bahudhā vipradhāvitān paryavasthāpayākhyāhi vibhīṣaṇam upasthitam
english: Quickly rally these thoroughly terrified ones who have fled in all directions, and announce that Vibhīṣaṇa has come."

sanskrit: sugrīveṇaivam uktas tu jāmbavān ṛkṣapārthivaḥ vānarān sāntvayām āsa saṃnivartya prahāvataḥ
english: Thus addressed by Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, calmed the fleeing monkeys and turned them back.

sanskrit: te nivṛttāḥ punaḥ sarve vānarās tyaktasaṃbhramāḥ ṛkṣarājavacaḥ śrutvā taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam
english: All those monkeys turned back once more, their agitation laid aside, having heard the words of the king of bears and having seen Vibhīṣaṇa himself.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā gātraṃ śaraiś citam lakṣmaṇasya ca dharmātmā babhūva vyathitendriyaḥ
english: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, seeing the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa covered with arrows, became distressed in all his senses.

sanskrit: jalaklinnena hastena tayor netre pramṛjya ca śokasaṃpīḍitamanā ruroda vilalāpa ca
english: Wiping their eyes with his hand moistened with tears, his heart crushed by grief, he wept and lamented aloud.

sanskrit: imau tau sattvasaṃpannau vikrāntau priyasaṃyugau imām avasthāṃ gamitau rākasaiḥ kūṭayodhibhiḥ
english: "These two, endowed with valor, brave in battle, fond of combat — they have been brought to this state by demons who fight with treachery.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ putreṇa me tena duṣputreṇa durātmanā rākṣasyā jihmayā buddhyā chalitāv ṛjuvikramau
english: These two, whose valor is straightforward, have been deceived by that wicked son of my brother, that evil-souled one, through the crooked cunning that is the way of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śarair imāv alaṃ viddhau rudhireṇa samukṣitau vasudhāyām ima suptau dṛśyete śalyakāv iva
english: Pierced through and through by arrows, drenched in blood, lying on the earth, these two appear like porcupines.

sanskrit: yayor vīryam upāśritya pratiṣṭhā kāṅkṣitā mayā tāv ubhau dehanāśāya prasuptau puruṣarṣabhau
english: Those two foremost of men, relying on whose valor I had hoped to establish myself — they both lie as if in the sleep that destroys the body.

sanskrit: jīvann adya vipanno 'smi naṣṭarājyamanorathaḥ prāptapratijñaś ca ripuḥ sakāmo rāvaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Living yet I am now ruined, my hope of regaining my kingdom lost, and the enemy Rāvaṇa made to fulfill his vow and have his desire."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānaṃ taṃ pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṃpanno harirājo 'bravīd idam
english: Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, possessed of fortitude, embraced the lamenting Vibhīṣaṇa and spoke these words:

sanskrit: rājyaṃ prāpsyasi dharmajña laṅkāyāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ rāvaṇaḥ saha putreṇa sa rājyaṃ neha lapsyate
english: "You shall obtain the kingdom in Laṅkā — of this there is no doubt, O knower of dharma. That Rāvaṇa, along with his son, shall not enjoy his kingdom here.

sanskrit: śarasaṃpīḍitāv etāv ubhau rāghavalakṣmaṇau tyaktvā mohaṃ vadhiṣyete sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
english: These two, Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa, though oppressed by arrows, will cast off their swoon and slay Rāvaṇa along with his host in battle."

sanskrit: tam evaṃ sāntvayitvā tu samāśvāsya ca rākṣasaṃ suṣeṇaṃ śvaśuraṃ pārśve sugrīvas tam uvāca ha
english: Having thus consoled and reassured the rākṣasa, Sugrīva spoke to Suṣeṇa, his father-in-law, who stood at his side:

sanskrit: saha śūrair harigaṇair labdhasaṃjñāv ariṃdamau gaccha tvaṃ bhrātarau gṛhya kiṣkindhāṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "Take the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, those tamers of foes when they regain consciousness, along with the host of brave monkeys, and go to Kiṣkindhā.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu rāvaṇaṃ hatvā saputraṃ sahabāndhavam maithilīm ānayiṣyāmi śakro naṣṭām iva śriyam
english: I, however, shall slay Rāvaṇa together with his son and kinsmen, and bring back the Maithilī, as Śakra [would recover] lost glory."

sanskrit: śrutvaitad vānarendrasya suṣeṇo vākyam abravīt devāsuraṃ mahāyuddham anubhūtaṃ sudāruṇam
english: Having heard this, Suṣeṇa spoke a reply to the lord of the vānaras: "I myself witnessed the great and utterly dreadful war between the gods and asuras,

sanskrit: tadā sma dānavā devāñ śarasaṃsparśakovidāḥ nijaghnuḥ śastraviduṣaś chādayanto muhur muhuḥ
english: When the dānavas, skilled in the touch of arrows, experienced in weapons, struck the gods repeatedly, covering them with shafts again and again.

sanskrit: tān ārtān naṣṭasaṃjñāṃś ca parāsūṃś ca bṛhaspatiḥ vidhyābhir mantrayuktābhir oṣadhībhiś cikitsati
english: Those afflicted ones, unconscious and seemingly dead, Bṛhaspati treated with incantations imbued with mantras, and with medicinal herbs.

sanskrit: tāny auṣadhāny ānayituṃ kṣīrodaṃ yāntu sāgaram javena vānarāḥ śīghraṃ saṃpāti panasādayaḥ
english: To fetch those herbs, let the monkeys — Saṃpāti, Panasa, and others — go swiftly with speed to the Milk Ocean.

sanskrit: harayas tu vijānanti pārvatī te mahauṣadhī saṃjīvakaraṇīṃ divyāṃ viśalyāṃ devanirmitām
english: The monkeys know of those great mountain-herbs — the divine Saṃjīvakaraṇī [life-restorer] and Viśalyā [arrow-extractor], fashioned by the gods.

sanskrit: candraś ca nāma droṇaś ca parvatau sāgarottame amṛtaṃ yatra mathitaṃ tatra te paramauṣadhī
english: [On] the mountains named Candra and Droṇa, foremost in the ocean — where the amṛta was churned forth — there those supreme medicinal herbs [grow].

sanskrit: te tatra nihite devaiḥ parvate paramauṣadhī ayaṃ vāyusuto rājan hanūmāṃs tatra gacchatu
english: Those supreme herbs placed there on the mountains by the gods — let this son of the Wind, Hanūmān, go there, O king."

sanskrit: etasminn antare vāyur meghāṃś cāpi savidyutaḥ paryasyan sāgare toyaṃ kampayann iva parvatān
english: At that very moment the wind swept through the clouds along with their lightning, and, stirring the waters of the ocean, seemed to shake the very mountains.

sanskrit: mahatā pakṣavātena sarve dvīpamahādrumāḥ nipetur bhagnaviṭapāḥ samūlā lavaṇāmbhasi
english: By the mighty gale of his wings, all the great island trees fell, their branches broken, with their roots, into the salt sea.

sanskrit: abhavan pannagās trastā bhoginas tatravāsinaḥ śīghraṃ sarvāṇi yādāṃsi jagmuś ca lavaṇārṇavam
english: The hooded serpents dwelling there were terrified, and all the creatures of the sea swiftly entered the salt ocean.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtad garuḍaṃ vainateyaṃ mahābalam vānarā dadṛśuḥ sarve jvalantam iva pāvakam
english: Then after a moment all the monkeys beheld Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, of great might, blazing as it were like fire.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya nāgās te vipradudruvuḥ yais tau satpuruṣau baddhau śarabhūtair mahābalau
english: Seeing him arrive, those nāgas that had bound the two noble men, who had become mighty arrows, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇaḥ kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā pratyabhinandya ca vimamarśa ca pāṇibhyāṃ mukhe candrasamaprabhe
english: Then Suparṇa [Garuḍa], seeing the two of the Kākutstha line, greeted them warmly, and stroked their faces — which shone like the moon — with both his hands.

sanskrit: vainateyena saṃspṛṣṭās tayoḥ saṃruruhur vraṇāḥ suvarṇe ca tanū snigdhe tayor āśu babhūvatuḥ
english: Touched by Vainateya [Garuḍa], their wounds closed up at once; their bodies became smooth and golden immediately.

sanskrit: tejo vīryaṃ balaṃ cauja utsāhaś ca mahāguṇāḥ pradarśanaṃ ca buddhiś ca smṛtiś ca dviguṇaṃ tayoḥ
english: Radiance, heroic energy, strength, vital power, and enterprise — those great qualities — as well as their perception, intelligence, and memory, were doubled in the two of them.

sanskrit: tāv utthāpya mahāvīryau garuḍo vāsavopamau ubhau tau sasvaje hṛṣṭau rāmaś cainam uvāca ha
english: Garuḍa raised up those two of great valor, who were equal to Vāsava [Indra], and embraced them both joyfully; then Rāma addressed him:

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād vyasanaṃ rāvaṇiprabhavaṃ mahat āvām iha vyatikrāntau śīghraṃ ca balinau kṛtau
english: "By your grace the great calamity arising from Rāvaṇa's son has been overcome by us here, and swiftly have we been made strong.

sanskrit: yathā tātaṃ daśarathaṃ yathājaṃ ca pitāmaham tathā bhavantam āsādya hṛṣayaṃ me prasīdati
english: Just as my heart rejoices on meeting my father Daśaratha and grandfather Aja, so too does it rejoice in meeting you — be gracious.

sanskrit: ko bhavān rūpasaṃpanno divyasraganulepanaḥ vasāno viraje vastre divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
english: Who are you, endowed with a beautiful form, wearing divine garlands and unguents, clothed in spotless garments, adorned with divine ornaments?"

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejā vainateyo mahābalaḥ patatrirājaḥ prītātmā harṣaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
english: Then Vainateya [Garuḍa], of great splendor and great might, king of birds, his heart full of affection, his eyes brimming with joy, spoke to him:

sanskrit: ahaṃ sakhā te kākutstha priyaḥ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ garutmān iha saṃprāpto yuvayoḥ sāhyakāraṇāt
english: "I am your friend, O Kākutstha — your dear prāṇa that moves outside the body. I am Garuṭmān, come here for the sake of helping you both.

sanskrit: asurā vā mahāvīryā dānavā vā mahābalāḥ surāś cāpi sagandharvāḥ puraskṛtya śatakratum
english: Neither the asuras of great valor, nor the dānavas of great power, nor even the gods along with the Gandharvas with the Hundred-Sacrificed Indra at their head —

sanskrit: nemaṃ mokṣayituṃ śaktāḥ śarabandhaṃ sudāruṇam māyā balād indrajitā nirmitaṃ krūrakarmaṇā
english: None of these would have been capable of releasing [you from] this arrow-bondage, so dreadful, constructed by the power of illusion by Indrajit of cruel deeds.

sanskrit: ete nāgāḥ kādraveyās tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāviṣolbaṇāḥ rakṣomāyā prabhāvena śarā bhūtvā tvadāśritāḥ
english: These nāgas, sons of Kadrū, with sharp fangs and venom overflowing, by the power of rākṣasa-illusion became arrows and clung to you.

sanskrit: sabhāgyaś cāsi dharmajña rāma satyaparākrama lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā samare ripughātinā
english: You are truly fortunate, O Rāma, knower of dharma, one whose valor is real, together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of foes in battle.

sanskrit: imaṃ śrutvā tu vṛttāntaṃ tvaramāṇo 'ham āgataḥ sahasā yuvayoḥ snehāt sakhitvam anupālayan
english: Having heard of this event, I came in haste, swiftly, out of affection for you both, honoring the bond of friendship.

sanskrit: mokṣitau ca mahāghorād asmāt sāyakabandhanāt apramādaś ca kartavyo yuvābhyāṃ nityam eva hi
english: And now that you have been released from this most terrible arrow-bondage, you both must always maintain vigilance without fail.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā rākṣasāḥ sarve saṃgrāme kūṭayodhinaḥ śūrāṇāṃ śuddhabhāvānāṃ bhavatām ārjavaṃ balam
english: By their very nature, all rākṣasas fight with treachery in battle; the strength of brave ones like you, who are pure in spirit, lies in straightforwardness.

sanskrit: tan na viśvasitavyaṃ vo rākṣasānāṃ raṇājire etenaivopamānena nityajihmā hi rākṣasāḥ
english: Therefore you must not trust rākṣasas on the battlefield — by this very [reasoning]: rākṣasas are always crooked."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rāmaṃ suparṇaḥ sumahābalaḥ pariṣvajya suhṛtsnigdham āpraṣṭum upacakrame
english: Having spoken thus, Suparṇa [Garuḍa] of very great power embraced Rāma with the affection of a dear friend, and then made ready to take his leave.

sanskrit: sakhe rāghava dharmajña ripūṇām api vatsala abhyanujñātum icchāmi gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: "Friend Rāghava, O knower of dharma, tender even toward enemies — I desire your leave; I shall go as I came.

sanskrit: bālavṛddhāvaśeṣāṃ tu laṅkāṃ kṛtvā śarormibhiḥ rāvaṇaṃ ca ripuṃ hatvā sītāṃ samupalapsyase
english: Having made Laṅkā desolate but for children and the aged with waves of arrows, and having slain the enemy Rāvaṇa, you shall recover Sītā."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ suparṇaḥ śīghravikramaḥ rāmaṃ ca virujaṃ kṛtvā madhye teṣāṃ vanaukasām
english: Having spoken these words, Suparṇa of swift motion, having made Rāma whole and free of wounds in the midst of those forest-dwellers,

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pariṣvajya ca vīryavān jagāmākāśam āviśya suparṇaḥ pavano yathā
english: Suparṇa, the valiant one, then circumambulated him and embraced him, entered the sky, and departed like the wind.

sanskrit: virujau rāghavau dṛṣṭvā tato vānarayūthapāḥ siṃhanādāṃs tadā nedur lāṅgūlaṃ dudhuvuś ca te
english: Then the leaders of the monkey troops, seeing the two Rāghavas healed of wounds, roared with lion-roars and waved their tails.

sanskrit: tato bherīḥ samājaghnur mṛdaṅgāṃś ca vyanādayan dadhmuḥ śaṅkhān saṃprahṛṣṭāḥ kṣvelanty api yathāpuram
english: Then they beat kettledrums and sounded the mṛdaṅgas, blew their conches in great exultation, and howled as was their wont.

sanskrit: āsphoṭyāsphoṭya vikrāntā vānarā nagayodhinaḥ drumān utpāṭya vividhāṃs tasthuḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: The valiant tree-fighting monkeys, slapping their arms in challenge again and again, uprooted various trees and stood ready by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: visṛjanto mahānādāṃs trāsayanto niśācarān laṅkādvārāṇy upājagmur yoddhukāmāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: The leaping monkeys, desirous of battle, emitting great roars and terrifying the night-wanderers, advanced toward the gates of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tatas tu bhīmas tumulo ninādo babhūva śākhāmṛgayūthapānām kṣaye nidāghasya yathā ghanānāṃ nādaḥ subhīmo nadatāṃ niśīthe
english: Then arose a terrible, tumultuous roar from the hosts of the monkey leaders — like the most fearsome sound of thunderclouds roaring at midnight in the waning of the summer heat.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sutumulaṃ śabdaṃ vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām nardatāṃ rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ tadā śuśrāva rāvaṇaḥ
english: The tumultuous sound of those swift-moving monkeys roaring together with the rākṣasas was then heard by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: snigdhagambhīranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā sa ninadaṃ bhṛśam sacivānāṃ tatas teṣāṃ madhye vacanam abravīt
english: Having listened to that roar, which was deep, resonant, and very powerful, he spoke a word in the midst of those his ministers:

sanskrit: yathāsau saṃprahṛṣṭānāṃ vānarāṇāṃ samutthitaḥ bahūnāṃ sumahān nādo meghānām iva garjatām
english: "This very great uproar of the many exultant monkeys has arisen, like the roaring of thunderclouds —

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ sumahatī prītir eteṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ tathā hi vipulair nādaiś cukṣubhe varuṇālayaḥ
english: Clearly these ones are in very great delight — of this there is no doubt; for indeed with their vast roars the abode of Varuṇa [the ocean] is shaken.

sanskrit: tau tu baddhau śarais tīṣkṇair bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau ayaṃ ca sumahān nādaḥ śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me
english: Yet the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa were bound with sharp arrows — and this very great uproar seems to arouse suspicion in me."

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ coktvā mantriṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ uvāca nairṛtāṃs tatra samīpaparivartinaḥ
english: Having spoken that word to his ministers, the lord of the rākṣasas then addressed the nairṛtas [demon-warriors] who attended nearby:

sanskrit: jñāyatāṃ tūrṇam etaṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vanacāriṇām śokakāle samutpanne harṣakāraṇam utthitam
english: "Let it be found out quickly — what cause of joy has arisen for all these forest-wanderers at a time when sorrow should have prevailed?"

sanskrit: tathoktās tena saṃbhrāntāḥ prākāram adhiruhya te dadṛśuḥ pālitāṃ senāṃ sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
english: So commanded by him, they hastened and climbed the rampart, and saw the army marshaled by the great-souled Sugrīva.

sanskrit: tau ca muktau sughoreṇa śarabandhena rāghavau samutthitau mahābhāgau viṣeduḥ prekṣya rākṣasāḥ
english: And seeing the two Rāghavas of great dignity freed from that most terrible arrow-bondage and risen up again, the rākṣasas were stricken with dismay.

sanskrit: saṃtrastahṛdayā sarve prākārād avaruhya te viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve rākṣasendram upasthitāḥ
english: All their hearts struck with fear, they descended from the rampart and stood before the lord of rākṣasas, every face cast down.

sanskrit: tad apriyaṃ dīnamukhā rāvaṇasya niśācarāḥ kṛtsnaṃ nivedayām āsur yathāvad vākyakovidāḥ
english: Those night-wanderers, skilled in speech, with wretched faces, reported to Rāvaṇa that unwelcome news fully and accurately:

sanskrit: yau tāv indrajitā yuddhe bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau nibaddhau śarabandhena niṣprakampabhujau kṛtau
english: "Those two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa who were bound in battle by Indrajit with the arrow-bondage, rendered immovable of arm —

sanskrit: vimuktau śarabandhena tau dṛśyete raṇājire pāśān iva gajau chittvā gajendrasamavikramau
english: — those two are seen freed from the arrow-bondage on the battlefield, like two great elephants equal in valor to lords of elephants having snapped their fetters."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ rākṣasendro mahābalaḥ cintāśokasamākrānto viṣaṇṇavadano 'bravīt
english: Hearing their words, the lord of rākṣasas of great power, overwhelmed by anxious grief, spoke with a downcast face:

sanskrit: ghorair dattavarair baddhau śarair āśīviṣomapaiḥ amoghaiḥ sūryasaṃkāśaiḥ pramathyendrajitā yudhi
english: "Bound by those terrible arrows bestowed by [divine] boons, equal in venom to the āśīviṣa serpents, unfailing, blazing like the sun — having been struck down in battle by Indrajit —

sanskrit: tam astrabandham āsādya yadi muktau ripū mama saṃśayastham idaṃ sarvam anupaśyāmy ahaṃ balam
english: If my foes have been freed after falling into that weapon-bondage, then I see all my [military] power as standing in doubt.

sanskrit: niṣphalāḥ khalu saṃvṛttāḥ śarā vāsukitejasaḥ ādattaṃ yais tu saṃgrāme ripūṇāṃ mama jīvitam
english: Truly those arrows of Vāsuki's [serpent-] power have proved fruitless — those with which the life of my enemies was seized in battle.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saṃkruddho niśvasann urago yathā abravīd rakṣasāṃ madhye dhūmrākṣaṃ nāma rākasaṃ
english: Having spoken thus, furious and hissing like a serpent, he spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas to the rākṣasa named Dhūmrākṣa:

sanskrit: balena mahatā yukto rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām tvaṃ vadhāyābhiniryāhi rāmasya saha vānaraiḥ
english: "Go forth, furnished with a great force of rākṣasas of terrible deeds, to slay Rāma together with the monkeys!"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dhūmrākṣo rākṣasendreṇa dhīmatā kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ saṃhṛṣṭo nirjagāma nṛpālayāt
english: Thus commanded by the wise lord of rākṣasas, Dhūmrākṣa made obeisance, and exulting he departed from the royal palace.

sanskrit: abhiniṣkramya taddvāraṃ balādhyakṣam uvāca ha tvarayasva balaṃ tūrṇaṃ kiṃ cireṇa yuyutsataḥ
english: Having gone out through the gate, he spoke to the marshal of troops: "Quickly muster the army — why this delay for one who desires battle?"

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣasya vacaḥ śrutvā balādhyakṣo balānugaḥ balam udyojayām āsa rāvaṇasyājñayā drutam
english: Hearing the words of Dhūmrākṣa, the marshal, who commanded the troops, quickly set the army in motion by Rāvaṇa's command.

sanskrit: te baddhaghaṇṭā balino ghorarūpā niśācarāḥ vinardamānāḥ saṃhṛṣṭā dhūmrākṣaṃ paryavārayan
english: Those powerful night-wanderers of dreadful forms, their bells fastened, roaring and exultant, surrounded Dhūmrākṣa.

sanskrit: vividhāyudhahastāś ca śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ gadābhiḥ paṭṭasair daṇḍair āyasair musalair bhṛśam
english: Bearing various weapons in their hands — holding lances and hammers — [armed] greatly with clubs, broadswords, iron staffs, maces,

sanskrit: parighair bhiṇḍipālaiś ca bhallaiḥ prāsaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ niryayū rākṣasā ghorā nardanto jaladā yathā
english: Iron bars, sling-stones, bhalla-arrows, javelins, and battle-axes — the terrible rākṣasas went forth roaring like thunderclouds.

sanskrit: rathaiḥ kavacinas tv anye dhvajaiś ca samalaṃkṛtaiḥ suvarṇajālavihitaiḥ kharaiś ca vividhānanaiḥ
english: Others, clad in armor on chariots adorned with banners, fitted with golden trelliswork, [drew by] asses of various faces,

sanskrit: hayaiḥ paramaśīghraiś ca gajendraiś ca madotkaṭaiḥ niryayū rākṣasavyāghrā vyāghrā iva durāsadāḥ
english: [Some drawn] by supremely swift horses and by maddened lordly elephants — those tiger-rākṣasas went forth, unapproachable as tigers.

sanskrit: vṛkasiṃhamukhair yuktaṃ kharaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ dhūmrākṣaḥ kharanisvanaḥ
english: Dhūmrākṣa, loud-braying as an ass, mounted a divine chariot yoked to asses with the faces of wolves and lions, adorned with gold.

sanskrit: sa niryāto mahāvīryo dhūmrākṣo rākṣasair vṛtaḥ prahasan paścimadvāraṃ hanūmān yatra yūthapaḥ
english: That great hero Dhūmrākṣa, surrounded by rākṣasas, went forth laughing toward the western gate, where Hanūmān was the troop-commander.

sanskrit: prayāntaṃ tu mahāghoraṃ rākṣasaṃ bhīmadarśanam antarikṣagatāḥ krūrāḥ śakunāḥ pratyavārayan
english: As that most dreadful rākṣasa of fearsome appearance proceeded forth, cruel birds moving through the sky obstructed his path.

sanskrit: rathaśīrṣe mahābhīmo gṛdhraś ca nipapāta ha dhvajāgre grathitāś caiva nipetuḥ kuṇapāśanāḥ
english: A most terrible vulture fell upon the top of his chariot, and carrion-eaters fell clustered at the tip of his banner-staff.

sanskrit: rudhirārdro mahāñ śvetaḥ kabandhaḥ patito bhuvi visvaraṃ cotsṛjan nādaṃ dhūmrākṣasya samīpataḥ
english: A great white headless trunk, drenched in blood, fell to the earth near Dhūmrākṣa, emitting a discordant cry.

sanskrit: vavarṣa rudhiraṃ devaḥ saṃcacāla ca medinī pratilomaṃ vavau vāyur nirghātasamanisvanaḥ timiraughāvṛtās tatra diśaś ca na cakāśire
english: The sky rained blood and the earth trembled; the wind blew in the wrong direction with a sound like a thunderbolt; the quarters there were wrapped in masses of darkness and did not shine forth.

sanskrit: sa tūtpātāṃs tato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasānāṃ bhayāvahān prādurbhūtān sughorāṃś ca dhūmrākṣo vyathito 'bhavat
english: Seeing those terrifying, most dreadful portents of evil manifested for the rākṣasas, Dhūmrākṣa was distressed.

sanskrit: tataḥ subhīmo bahubhir niśācarair vṛto 'bhiniṣkramya raṇotsuko balī dadarśa tāṃ rāghavabāhupālitāṃ samudrakalpāṃ bahuvānarīṃ camūm
english: Then the most terrible and mighty one, eager for battle, went forth surrounded by many night-wanderers, and beheld that vast army of many monkeys, protected by the arm of Rāghava, vast as the ocean.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣaṃ prekṣya niryāntaṃ rākṣasaṃ bhīmanisvanam vinedur vānarāḥ sarve prahṛṣṭā yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa the rākṣasa, of fearsome sound, going forth, all the monkeys, joyful and eager for battle, roared out.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ saṃjajñe harirakṣasām anyonyaṃ pādapair ghorair nighnataṃ śūlamudgaraiḥ
english: Then arose a tumultuous battle between the monkeys and the rākṣasas, each striking the other with terrible trees and with lances and hammers.

sanskrit: rākṣasair vānarā ghorā vinikṛttāḥ samantataḥ vānarai rākṣasāś cāpi drumair bhūmau samīkṛtāḥ
english: The terrible monkeys were cut down on all sides by the rākṣasas; and the rākṣasas in turn were leveled to the ground by the monkeys with trees.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś cāpi saṃkruddhā vānarān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vivyadhur ghorasaṃkāśaiḥ kaṅkapatrair ajihmagaiḥ
english: And the rākṣasas, enraged, pierced the monkeys with sharp arrows — those of terrible appearance, feathered with heron-feathers, flying straight.

sanskrit: te gadābhiś ca bhīmābhiḥ paṭṭasaiḥ kūṭamudgaraiḥ ghoraiś ca parighaiś citrais triśūlaiś cāpi saṃśitaiḥ
english: With those dreadful clubs and broadswords, iron hammers, with terrible iron bars of various kinds, and with sharpened tridents —

sanskrit: vidāryamāṇā rakṣobhir vānarās te mahābalāḥ amarṣāj janitoddharṣāś cakruḥ karmāṇy abhītavat
english: Though torn apart by the rākṣasas, those monkeys of great might, their spirit roused by indignation, performed their deeds without fear.

sanskrit: śaranirbhinnagātrās te śūlanirbhinnadehinaḥ jagṛhus te drumāṃs tatra śilāś ca hariyūthapāḥ
english: Their bodies pierced through with arrows, their frames transfixed with lances, those leaders of monkey troops nonetheless seized trees and boulders there.

sanskrit: te bhīmavegā harayo nardamānās tatas tataḥ mamanthū rākṣasān bhīmān nāmāni ca babhāṣire
english: Those monkeys of terrible velocity, roaring here and there, churned through the dreadful rākṣasas and called out their own names.

sanskrit: tad babhūvādbhutaṃ ghoraṃ yuddhaṃ vānararakṣasām śilābhir vividhābhiś ca bahuśākhaiś ca pādapaiḥ
english: The battle between the monkeys and rākṣasas was wondrous and dreadful, fought with boulders of various kinds and with trees of many branches.

sanskrit: rākṣasā mathitāḥ ke cid vānarair jitakāśibhiḥ vavarṣū rudhiraṃ ke cin mukhai rudhirabhojanāḥ
english: Some rākṣasas, crushed by the victorious-seeming monkeys, gushed blood; some, blood-eaters, rained it from their mouths.

sanskrit: pārśveṣu dāritāḥ ke cit ke cid rāśīkṛtā drumaiḥ śilābhiś cūrṇitāḥ ke cit ke cid dantair vidāritāḥ
english: Some were ripped open in the flanks, some were piled in heaps by trees, some were pulverized by boulders, and some were torn apart by teeth.

sanskrit: dhvajair vimathitair bhagnaiḥ kharaiś ca vinipātitaiḥ rathair vidhvaṃsitaiś cāpi patitai rajanīcaraiḥ
english: With banners shattered and broken, with asses brought down and slain, with chariots smashed and destroyed, with night-wanderers fallen —

sanskrit: vānarair bhīmavikrāntair āplutyāplutya vegitaiḥ rākṣasāḥ karajais tīkṣṇair mukheṣu vinikartitāḥ
english: The rākṣasas were slashed in the face by the sharp nails of the swift-moving monkeys of terrible valor, who bounded upon them again and again.

sanskrit: vivarṇavadanā bhūyo viprakīrṇaśiroruhāḥ mūḍhāḥ śoṇitagandhena nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Their faces discolored, their hair disheveled, stupefied by the smell of blood, they fell to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: naye tu paramakruddhā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ talair evābhidhāvanti vajrasparśasamair harīn
english: Yet some rākṣasas, supremely enraged and of terrible valor, attacked the monkeys with open palms equal to thunderbolts in their touch.

sanskrit: vanarair āpatantas te vegitā vegavattaraiḥ muṣṭibhiś caraṇair dantaiḥ pādapaiś cāpapothitāḥ
english: Those [rākṣasas] who charged were beaten back by the swifter-moving monkeys with fists, feet, teeth, and trees.

sanskrit: sanyaṃ tu vidrutaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhūmrākṣo rākṣasarṣabhaḥ krodhena kadanaṃ cakre vānarāṇāṃ yuyutsatām
english: Seeing the army in rout, Dhūmrākṣa, foremost of rākṣasas, in his anger wrought carnage among the battle-seeking monkeys.

sanskrit: prāsaiḥ pramathitāḥ ke cid vānarāḥ śoṇitasravāḥ mudgarair āhatāḥ ke cit patitā dharaṇītale
english: Some monkeys were struck down with javelins and streamed with blood; some struck with hammers fell to the ground.

sanskrit: parighair mathitaḥ ke cid bhiṇḍipālair vidāritāḥ paṭṭasair āhatāḥ ke cid vihvalanto gatāsavaḥ
english: Some were crushed with iron bars, some were split open with sling-stones, some were struck with broadswords and expired in agony.

sanskrit: ke cid vinihatā bhūmau rudhirārdrā vanaukasaḥ ke cid vidrāvitā naṣṭāḥ saṃkruddhai rākṣasair yudhi
english: Some of the forest-dwellers lay slain on the ground, drenched in blood; some were routed and lost sight of, scattered by the furious rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: vibhinnahṛdayāḥ ke cid ekapārśvena śāyitāḥ vidāritāstraśūlai ca ke cid āntrair vinisrutāḥ
english: Some lay with hearts split open, fallen on one side; some were torn open by weapons and lances, their entrails spilling out.

sanskrit: tat subhīmaṃ mahad yuddhaṃ harirākasa saṃkulam prababhau śastrabahulaṃ śilāpādapasaṃkulam
english: That most terrible great battle, crowded with monkeys and rākṣasas, blazed forth — abounding in weapons, thronging with boulders and trees.

sanskrit: dhanurjyātantrimadhuraṃ hikkātālasamanvitam mandrastanitasaṃgītaṃ yuddhagāndharvam ābabhau
english: It blazed as a gandharva-music of war — sweet with the strain of bowstrings, accompanied by yells and the beat of time, a symphony of deep rumbling thunder.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣas tu dhanuṣpāṇir vānarān raṇamūrdhani hasan vidrāvayām āsa diśas tāñ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: But Dhūmrākṣa, bow in hand, laughing, scattered the monkeys in all directions at the forefront of battle with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣeṇārditaṃ sainyaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛśya mārutiḥ abhyavartata saṃkruddhaḥ pragṛhya vipulāṃ śilām
english: Seeing the army tormented and afflicted by Dhūmrākṣa, Māruti [Hanūmān] came forward in great fury, grasping an enormous boulder.

sanskrit: krodhād dviguṇatāmrākṣaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ śilāṃ tāṃ pātayām āsa dhūmrākṣasya rathaṃ prati
english: His eyes doubly reddened with rage, his valor equal to his father's, he hurled that boulder against the chariot of Dhūmrākṣa.

sanskrit: āpatantīṃ śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā gadām udyamya saṃbhramāt rathād āplutya vegena vasudhāyāṃ vyatiṣṭhata
english: Seeing the boulder rushing down, Dhūmrākṣa in alarm lifted his mace, leaped swiftly from his chariot, and stood on the ground.

sanskrit: sā pramathya rathaṃ tasya nipapāta śilābhuvi sacakrakūbaraṃ sāśvaṃ sadhvajaṃ saśarāsanam
english: That boulder, having smashed his chariot, fell upon the stony ground along with its wheels and pole, its horses, its banner, and its bow.

sanskrit: sa bhaṅktvā tu rathaṃ tasya hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ rakṣasāṃ kadanaṃ cakre saskandhaviṭapair drumaiḥ
english: Having shattered his chariot, Hanūmān son of the Wind then wrought carnage among the rākṣasas with trees bearing their branches and boughs.

sanskrit: vibhinnaśiraso bhūtvā rākṣasāḥ śoṇitokṣitāḥ drumair pramathitāś cānye nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Their heads split open, the rākṣasas, drenched in blood, and others crushed by the trees, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: vidrāvya rākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ gireḥ śikharam ādāya dhūmrākṣam abhidudruve
english: Routing the rākṣasa army, Hanūmān son of the Wind took a mountain peak and rushed at Dhūmrākṣa.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ dhūmrākṣo gadām udyamya vīryavān vinardamānaḥ sahasā hanūmantam abhidravat
english: Seeing him charging, Dhūmrākṣa, valiant, mace raised, suddenly rushed roaring at Hanūmān.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhas tu vegena gadāṃ tāṃ bahukaṇṭakām pātayām āsa dhūmrākṣo mastake tu hanūmataḥ
english: Then in rage Dhūmrākṣa with great force brought down that spike-studded mace upon the head of Hanūmān.

sanskrit: tāḍitaḥ sa tayā tatra gadayā bhīmarūpayā sa kapir mārutabalas taṃ prahāram acintayan dhūmrākṣasya śiro madhye giriśṛṅgam apātayat
english: Struck by that mace of fearsome form, the monkey of wind-like might disregarded that blow and brought the mountain peak down on the very crown of Dhūmrākṣa's head.

sanskrit: sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo giriśṛṅgeṇa tāḍitaḥ papāta sahasā bhūmau vikīrṇa iva parvataḥ
english: His every limb convulsed, struck down by the mountain peak, he fell suddenly to the earth like a mountain shattered asunder.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ trastāḥ praviviśur laṅkāṃ vadhyamānāḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa slain, the surviving night-wanderers, terrified, fled back into Laṅkā even as they were being cut down by the leaping monkeys.

sanskrit: sa tu pavanasuto nihatya śatruṃ kṣatajavahāḥ saritaś ca saṃvikīrya ripuvadhajanitaśramo mahātmā mudam agamat kapibhiś ca pūjyamānaḥ
english: The great-souled son of the Wind, having slain the enemy and scattered rivers of blood from wounds, wearied by the slaughter of the foe, rejoiced and was honored by the monkeys.
